questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A place i would not otherwise experience. 
Interesting courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Ilisimatusarfik was very flexible, welcoming and always ready to help and give advise.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A volunteer at the University was very helpful in the beginning and made sure we had access to all the necessary.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was invited to an intro meeting and was connected to the very nice volunteer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get housing through KAF. Try to apply you migth be lucky as well. Otherwise you can find facebook groups where you can find privat housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Even though you live "far" from campus the busses are very accessible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very cheap if you get housing through KAF. Otherwise it's around 3500 - 4000DKK

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After my nomination from KU I received an e-mail from the contact at Ilisimatusarfik. In the e-mail there was a link an application that i just had to fill in. Very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help via e-mail with Per from Ilisimatusarfik. He is very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the ones I planned to register for were not available that semester - but it was very easy to register. I could choose what ever I found interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect that the courses you find before going might not be available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one course where the academic level did'nt meet my expectation, but the two others did.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style is a bit different than what I am used to and you are expected to share your own views and experiences.
I was interesting to try something else and be involved in a different way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sprog i Samfundet
Kultur - og samfundsforhold efter kolonitiden 
The Politics of the Climate and Environmental Change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Kultur - og samfundsforhold!  if you speak/understand danish and want to learn more about colonial dynamics, struktures both historic and present. Very relevant and so important knowledge to have!

questions.answer:
If you get student housing that is very cheap. 
Food is not cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talks, food events, cake, greenlandic classes(!!) and coffee for exchange student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the Greenlandic classes! Volunteer at the Røde Kors thrift store or the soup kitchen. Amazing way to meet people. Go to concerts, festivals etc at Katuaq.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you have the money I would highly recommend going taking the ferry up of down the coast. Otherwise there are amazing hikes around town, you should also go on boat trips around the fjord, try saunagus at Inukhostel or Minguik.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me as a Dane it was easy to some extendbecuase of the language ect, but of course there were a period of adjustment.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The sound volume when speaking can seem very lloud to locals.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmness, welcoming people<3

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Life is slow paced, but there is a lot of thing to do!
- You can't hide in class and will get to know the teachers.
- Most beautiful place and culture that you will not regret experiencing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have to have cash to be able to take the bus. Good to know when you arrive in the airport because you have to walk/ take a taxi otherwise.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling very far from my friend and family in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
